messages.subject: line lenght estimation
parts:
dear colleagues,

We used Distance to calculate the density of houbara bustards during line
transect surveys in the wild.
The density calculated was D= 0.101 indiv/kmsq, with %CV=18 and L=16059km.
My question is: is there a mean to calculate the effort to produce (or L)
if this density is reduced by half (say 0.05 indiv/kmsq), and with
conserving the same %cv?
The use of the equation (7.1), p 303 in the DISTANCE book, to estimate the
line length to be surveyed is to apply when a small-scale pilot study was
already made and takes not account of for variation of D, or?
Sorry if I missed or misundertood some Distance book instructions.
Many thanks
